name: Lina
bio: My name is Lina Couto Cunha, and I am a teacher at the Portuguese School of Nossa Senhora de Fátima in Vancouver. I teach A1/A2-level students between the ages of 12 and 16.

I was born and raised in the Azores, where I developed an early and strong connection to education and the Portuguese language. I completed my Bachelor’s degree in Early Childhood Education at the University of the Azores, which provided me with a solid foundation in pedagogy, child development, and educational practice.

After moving to Canada, I continued to expand my education by completing an equivalency in Early Childhood Education and Care through Capilano University in British Columbia. This additional training allowed me to fully integrate into the Canadian education system and develop a deeper understanding of practices that support diversity and inclusion in early childhood settings.

I currently work as the Coordinator of the Supported Child Development Program in the Tri-Cities region, where I collaborate with families, childcare centres, schools, and professionals from a variety of fields to promote the development and inclusion of children with diverse needs. In parallel, I teach at the Portuguese School of Nossa Senhora de Fátima, where, driven by my passion for the Portuguese language, I prepare young students for the CAPLE exams, while supporting their academic and cultural development.
